title: Getting a GRIP on Graph-Based Search for Learned Sparse Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2610.30425v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Learned sparse retrieval (LSR) has recently gained traction in the information retrieval community for the ability to combine the generalization capabilities of neural representations with the interpretability of keyword-based search. A number of recent works have demonstrated that inverted indexes, when appropriately modified for learned sparse embeddings, achieve state-of-the-art recall-latency tradeoffs for LSR, often outperforming graph-based indexes by substantial margins in latency at a fixed recall target. As a result, the community has generally concluded that graph-based approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search is inferior to inverted indexes for LSR. This paper challenges this conventional wisdom. translated_title: 掌握学习型稀疏检索中基于图的搜索（Getting a GRIP）
translated_abstract: 学习型稀疏检索（LSR）近年来在信息检索领域受到广泛关注，因为它能够将神经表示的泛化能力与基于关键词搜索的可解释性相结合。近期多项研究表明，倒排索引在针对学习型稀疏嵌入进行适当修改后，能够为LSR实现最先进的召回率-延迟权衡，在固定召回率目标下，其延迟通常大幅优于基于图的索引。因此，学界普遍认为，对于LSR而言，基于图的近似最近邻（ANN）搜索不如倒排索引。本文挑战了这一传统观点。我们的核心洞察是：虽然将标准的基于图的ANN索引直接应用于稀疏向量会导致缺乏竞争力的性能，但通过将倒排索引的优势融入图搜索中，我们可以克服这些不足……
tldr: 本文挑战了“图索引在学习型稀疏检索中劣于倒排索引”的传统观点，提出将倒排索引的优势融入图搜索，从而使基于图的ANN方法在LSR任务上也能达到有竞争力的性能。
en_tdlr: This paper challenges the conventional wisdom that graph-based ANN search is inferior to inverted indexes for learned sparse retrieval, demonstrating that by infusing the strengths of inverted indexes into graph search, graph-based methods can achieve competitive performance for LSR.
